name: dm_ima_measure_on_device_remove
prose: Precondition: md is a valid mapped_device whose ima.active_table and ima.inactive_table device_metadata and hash fields are each either NULL or a kmalloc'd buffer with its recorded length, and md->ima.dm_version_str_len is set. Postcondition: returns no value. (1) If the device_table_data allocation fails it jumps to exit. (2) If the capacity-string allocation fails it frees device_table_data and jumps to exit. (3) Otherwise it builds a record from the version string, whichever of the active/inactive device metadata and hashes are non-NULL, then "remove_all=y;" or "remove_all=n;" and the capacity string. If none of the four buffers is non-NULL it instead rewrites the record as name=<name>,uuid=<uuid>;device_remove=no_data; (allocating name and uuid first); if that allocation fails it jumps to error and no measurement is made. Otherwise it calls dm_ima_measure_data("dm_device_remove", ...). Label error frees device_table_data and capacity_str. Label exit is reached by every path of the function (it has no other return), and there it frees the active device_metadata and hash, frees the inactive device_metadata and hash only when the pointer differs from the active one, calls dm_ima_reset_data(md) and frees dev_name and dev_uuid.
note: Reviewer claim (alloc failure returns early without freeing/reset) is wrong: dm-ima.c:30-32 goto exit and 35-37 free device_table_data then goto exit; exit (119-134) frees the md buffers and calls dm_ima_reset_data. On the capacity failure capacity_str is NULL (dm_ima_alloc_and_copy_capacity_str returns -ENOMEM only when the allocation returned NULL). Old prose wrongly said measurement emitted whenever both allocs succeed; name/uuid alloc failure at line 98 skips it. Real source at line 466 of the file.

name: dm_integrity_map_continue
prose: Precondition: dio is the per-bio data of a bio submitted to the dm-integrity target, dio->ic points to an initialized target, dio->op and dio->range.logical_sector are set; from_map is true when called from the map routine (where sleeping is not allowed). The target may already be in a failed state. Postcondition: returns no value. (1) If the bio needs synchronous I/O (internal hash with a read, or a discard in a mode other than 'D') and from_map is true, it queues dio->work on ic->offload_wq and returns. (2) Under ic->endio_wait.lock, if dm_integrity_failed(ic) is nonzero it unlocks, calls do_endio(ic, bio) and returns. (3) In mode 'J' for non-discard bios, a write is clipped to the free journal space; if none is free it is offloaded to ic->wait_wq when from_map, else it sleeps and retries; otherwise it consumes journal entries (updating free_sectors, free_section, free_section_entry, n_uncommitted_sections, journal nodes), unlocks and goes to the journal read/write path; a read is clipped to the contiguous journal nodes. (4) If the range cannot be added to the in-progress tree and from_map is true, the bio is offloaded to ic->wait_wq; otherwise it waits for the range (with one-block size when the read hit the journal) and, if the journal node changed, removes the range and retries. (5) In mode 'J', a discard whose range overlaps journal nodes causes the range to be removed, the commit and writer workqueues to be flushed and the sequence retried once. (6) If a journal read hit exists or after jumping to journal_read_write, __journal_read_write is called: when it returns nonzero the whole locking sequence is retried, otherwise do_endio_flush(ic, dio) is called. (7) In mode 'B' a write or discard whose range is not entirely set in may_write_bitmap is queued on the bitmap block's bio_queue and returns. (8) Otherwise the bio is redirected to the underlying device with bi_end_io = integrity_end_io and submitted; discards in non-'D' modes first run integrity_metadata and flush buffers and are submitted with in_flight 1; a synchronous read waits for completion and then either skips the check (only dec_in_flight) when SB_FLAG_RECALCULATING is set and the range extends beyond recalc_sector, or in mode 'B' when the recalc bitmap is not all clear for the range, or when bio->bi_status is nonzero, else runs integrity_metadata; a non-synchronous bio queues integrity_metadata on ic->metadata_wq.
note: Reviewers: (a) 'precondition says device not failed' -- old prose already said the device may be failed; fixed to list the failure path first (2300-2311 region, source 167-171). (b) skip_check also on SB_FLAG_RECALCULATING with range beyond recalc_sector: right (source 345-347), old prose only mentioned recalc bitmap; fixed. Also the bi_status error case goes to dec_in_flight (354-358). Source line 2351 of the file; packet slice started mid-file but function fully read.

name: dm_integrity_resume
prose: Precondition: ti->private points to a fully constructed dm_integrity_c (ic->sb and ic->sb_copy valid) whose target is suspended. Postcondition: returns no value. It clears ic->wrote_to_journal, re-reads the superblock (a read failure is reported through dm_integrity_io_error and processing continues). If superblock_changed(ic) it restores ic->sb from ic->sb_copy, logs an error, records -EINVAL via dm_integrity_io_error and jumps to skip_writes. Else if ic->mode == 'R' it also jumps to skip_writes. Otherwise: if the RECALCULATING/DISCARD_KEYED flags it wants are not all set in the on-disk flags it sets them and writes the superblock; if ic->provided_data_sectors differs from the old value it (for a grown size in mode 'B' with SB_FLAG_DIRTY_BITMAP set and matching log2_blocks_per_bitmap_bit) extends the on-disk bitmap, then stores the new provided_data_sectors in the superblock and writes it. Then, if SB_FLAG_DIRTY_BITMAP is set in the superblock: it reads the bitmap blocks; in mode 'B', if the bitmap geometry matches and reset_recalculate_flag is clear it copies the bitmap into recalc_bitmap and may_write_bitmap and, when the bitmap is not all clear, sets RECALCULATING with recalc_sector 0; otherwise it stores the new geometry, sets all bits in recalc_bitmap, may_write_bitmap and the journal bitmap, writes the bitmap blocks and sets RECALCULATING with recalc_sector 0; in mode 'B' SB_FLAG_DIRTY_BITMAP stays set and no journal replay occurs. In other modes it sets RECALCULATING with recalc_sector 0 when the geometry mismatches or the bitmap is not all clear or reset_recalculate_flag is set, calls init_journal and replay_journal and clears SB_FLAG_DIRTY_BITMAP. In both modes it then writes the superblock. If SB_FLAG_DIRTY_BITMAP is clear it calls replay_journal, sets RECALCULATING with recalc_sector 0 if reset_recalculate_flag is set, and in mode 'B' sets SB_FLAG_DIRTY_BITMAP, stores the geometry, writes the superblock, clears the three bitmaps and, if RECALCULATING is set and recalc_sector < provided_data_sectors, sets the bits from recalc_sector to the end and writes the bitmap blocks. Next, if RECALCULATING is set it queues recalc_work on ic->recalc_wq when recalc_sector < provided_data_sectors, or when it is greater clamps recalc_sector to provided_data_sectors and calls recalc_write_super. At skip_writes (reached from both early exits and by fallthrough) it sets up ic->reboot_notifier and calls register_reboot_notifier under WARN_ON. Superblock write failures are reported via dm_integrity_io_error.
note: Reviewer claims: (1) 'journal replayed but modes R and dirty-bitmap B skip replay' -- right as to the old wording; now stated per branch (source 410-411, 439-475 vs 479-480). (2) 'mode B dirty-bitmap path does not clear SB_FLAG_DIRTY_BITMAP; notifier registered on skip_writes' -- right (lines 465-475 clear only in non-B; 522-526). (3) prose omits RECALCULATING on geometry mismatch in non-B -- right (466-471), added. Source line 3889.

name: dm_integrity_ctr
prose: Precondition: ti is a dm_target under construction; argv holds argc strings with argc > DIRECT_ARGUMENTS (4): device, offset, tag size (or "-"), mode, then a feature-argument count and the optional arguments. Postcondition: returns 0 with ti->private set to a newly kzalloc'd dm_integrity_c that has the data device (and optional meta device) held through dm_get_device, mode (J, B, D, R or I), start, tag_size, sectors_per_block, optional parameters, internal hash and journal mac set up, workqueues, mempools, dm-io client, superblock buffer (if the superblock magic is missing, then in modes other than 'R' the area must be all zero, else -EINVAL "The device is not initialized"; initialize_superblock is then called and, in modes other than 'R', the new superblock is written later), bufio client, journal (modes other than 'R' and 'I'), bitmaps in mode 'B', sb_copy, max_io_len and flush/discard bios configured, and an audit log of success. Returns -EINVAL with ti->error "Invalid argument count" when argc <= 4 and -ENOMEM with "Cannot allocate integrity context" when the context allocation fails (both before ti->private is set). Every later failure (bad device, bad number or option, inconsistent options such as bitmap mode without internal hash or inline mode restrictions, superblock mismatches, allocation failures, recalculate with HMAC disabled returning -EOPNOTSUPP, etc.) sets ti->error, records the audit-log failure, calls dm_integrity_dtr(ti) itself to release everything acquired so far, and returns the error code held in r (the value returned by the failing call, or the -EINVAL/-ENOMEM/-EOPNOTSUPP set at that point).
note: Packet name 'integrity_ctr' is invented; real function is dm_integrity_ctr (file lines 4788-5501), slice cut the head. The old prose claimed cleanup is left to the caller's cleanup path: wrong, the bad label (5497-5500) calls dm_integrity_dtr(ti) before returning r. Note the early two returns before ti->private is set do not call dtr. Not verified in detail: whether dtr frees ic itself.

name: dm_stripe_init
prose: Precondition: called at module initialization, before the striped target is registered; dm_stripe_wq is a global that this function writes. Postcondition: allocates the global workqueue dm_stripe_wq with alloc_workqueue; if that returns NULL it returns -ENOMEM without registering the target. Otherwise it calls dm_register_target(&stripe_target); if that returns a negative value it destroys dm_stripe_wq, logs "target registration failed" and returns that negative value; otherwise it returns the non-negative value r from dm_register_target unchanged.
note: Contract dropped: function touches a global and calls other functions, so no contract. Reviewers: round 1/15 'contract weaker than prose' -- moot with empty contract. Prose precise: dm-stripe.c:749-758. Does not claim dm_stripe_wq is reset to NULL after destroy (it is not), the old prose said 'leaving no workqueue allocated' which is true only in the sense it is destroyed, pointer left dangling; removed.

name: int_log
prose: Precondition: base > 1 and n + base - 1 does not overflow unsigned int (the dm_div_up macro adds base - 1 to n); with base == 0 the division is by zero and with base == 1 n never decreases so the loop does not terminate. Postcondition: returns 0 when n <= 1; otherwise returns the number of times n must be replaced by ceil(n / base) until it is at most 1, which is between 1 and 32 for base >= 2. It reads and writes no global state.
contract: /*@ requires base > 1; requires n <= 4294967296 - base; ensures ((n <= 1) <==> (result == 0)) && ((n > 1) ==> (result >= 1 && result <= 32)); */
note: Reviewer 'prose says always returns 0' is stale; current prose already says 0 only for n<=1 (dm-table.c:775-780). Contract: result bounded to 1..32 for n>1 since each step at least halves n for base>=2 (n<=2^32-1 gives at most 32 steps). Exact ceiling-log not expressible without a logic function.

name: dm_table_determine_type
prose: Precondition: t is a valid dm_table with a valid t->md. If t->type is already set it must not be DM_TYPE_DAX_BIO_BASED (BUG_ON), and if t->type is DM_TYPE_NONE the table must contain at least one target or one hybrid target (otherwise BUG_ON(!request_based) fires after both flags stay zero). Postcondition: (1) if t->type is preset to DM_TYPE_BIO_BASED it takes the bio-based verification path; if preset to another type it goes to the request-based verification. (2) Otherwise it scans the targets; if both bio-based and request-based targets are found it logs and returns -EINVAL leaving t->type unchanged. Hybrid-only tables take request-based when the live md type is request-based, else bio-based. (3) Bio-based path: sets t->type = DM_TYPE_BIO_BASED, upgrades it to DM_TYPE_DAX_BIO_BASED if dm_table_supports_dax(t, device_not_dax_capable) is true or if the device list is empty and the live md type is DM_TYPE_DAX_BIO_BASED, and returns 0. (4) Request-based path: sets t->type = DM_TYPE_REQUEST_BASED (unless already preset), then returns -EINVAL if num_targets > 1; if the device list is empty it takes dm_get_live_table(), copies the live table's type into t->type when a live table exists, releases it with dm_put_live_table, and returns 0; otherwise it returns -EINVAL when there is no immutable target, when the immutable target's max_io_len is nonzero, or when the target has no iterate_devices or iterate_devices reports a non-request-stackable device; else returns 0. On the request-based -EINVAL returns t->type has already been set (to DM_TYPE_REQUEST_BASED unless it was preset).
note: Reviewers: (1) t->type is set to REQUEST_BASED before the verify_rq_based -EINVAL returns -- right (line 847, 856-886). (2) 'omits BUG_ON precondition for DAX preset' -- wrong for the current prose, which states it; kept (line 803). (3) 'omits -EINVAL when immutable target type lacks iterate_devices' -- right (line 882), added. Contract left empty: reads/modifies table struct. Source line 915.

name: process_vdo_message
prose: Precondition: vdo points to a valid vdo, argc >= 1 and argv holds at least argc NUL-terminated strings (argv[0] is read unconditionally). Postcondition: if argv[0] equals "dump" (case-insensitive) it returns vdo_dump(vdo, argc, argv, "dmsetup message"). Otherwise, when argc == 1, "dump-on-shutdown" sets vdo->dump_on_shutdown to true and returns 0, and "index-close", "index-create", "index-disable" or "index-enable" returns vdo_message_dedupe_index(vdo->hash_zones, argv[0]); none of these touch vdo->processing_message. For any other message, if atomic_cmpxchg of vdo->processing_message from 0 to 1 finds a nonzero value it returns -EBUSY without changing it; otherwise it calls process_vdo_message_locked(vdo, argc, argv), then after smp_wmb() sets vdo->processing_message back to 0 and returns that call's result, which is 0 for "compression on"/"compression off" (argc == 2) and -EINVAL for any other message or a bad compression argument. The function takes no locks or references of its own; the returns of vdo_dump and vdo_message_dedupe_index are not examined here.
note: Reviewers: (1) VDO status vs errno -- the locked helper only returns 0 or -EINVAL (dm-vdo-target.c:1017-1038); old prose's 'VDO status code' for that helper was wrong. (2) -EBUSY only on the generic path, dump/index/dump-on-shutdown bypass: right and already reflected (915-930 vs 932). (3) process_vdo_message_locked can return -EINVAL: right, added. Source line 1040 (actual 1045 in this tree).

name: parse_device_config
prose: Precondition: argc/argv hold the dmsetup table values, ti is the target being constructed (ti->len and ti->table valid) and config_ptr points to writable storage. Postcondition: on success it returns 0 (VDO_SUCCESS), stores a newly allocated device_config in *config_ptr with the parent device opened via dm_get_device into owned_device, and (for version 0) physical_blocks derived from the device size. On failure it does not set *config_ptr and returns: VDO_BAD_CONFIGURATION for a logical size not a multiple of 4096, argc == 0, an allocation failure, a failed string copy or number parse, a bad block size, a pool-name position mismatch, inconsistent zone counts, a block-map cache too small for the logical zones, or a failed dm_get_device; or the nonzero value returned by get_version_number or parse_optional_arguments (both return VDO_BAD_CONFIGURATION when they fail). Every failure after the config allocation frees the config (and puts the device if opened) through handle_parse_error and stores a static message in ti->error (for the early size/argc/alloc failures the config is NULL, so only the message is stored).
note: Packet name 'parse_vdo_table_line' does not exist in the source; the real function is parse_device_config (file lines 699-888) -- slice cut the head. Re-verified returns at 970-1130 of dump and 828-888 of file. Dropped first prose claim 'well-formed table line' as a precondition (not required). Contract empty: pointer args.

name: get_big_field
prose: Precondition: size < 64, (offset % 8) + size <= 64, and the 8 bytes starting at memory + offset/8 are readable. Postcondition: returns the size-bit field that starts at bit position offset of memory, where bit k of the buffer is bit (k % 8) of byte k/8 and the field is read little-endian with its lowest bit at offset; the result is 0 when size is 0. Reads memory and writes nothing.
note: Checked against delta-index.c:561-567. Same as before apart from the bit-numbering clarification. Pointer parameter, so no contract.

name: set_big_field
prose: Precondition: size < 64, (offset % 8) + size <= 64, value < (1 << size) (a value with higher bits set would corrupt the bits above the field), and the 8 bytes starting at memory + offset/8 are readable and writable. Postcondition: the size bits of memory starting at bit position offset equal value and the other bits of those 8 bytes are written back unchanged (the function does a read-modify-write of 8 bytes).
note: Checked against delta-index.c:569-579: data &= ~mask<<shift; data |= value<<shift; put_unaligned_le64. Pointer parameter, no contract.

name: set_zero
prose: Precondition: every byte of memory that overlaps the bit range [offset, offset + size) is writable. Postcondition: if size is 0 nothing is read or written. Otherwise every bit of memory in [offset, offset + size) is 0 (bit k of the buffer is bit k % 8 of byte k/8) and all other bits are unchanged; only the bytes overlapping the range are accessed.
note: Traced the three cases: first partial byte (count = min(size, 8 - shift)), whole middle bytes while size > 8, last partial byte via *addr &= 0xFF << size (also zeroes a whole byte when exactly 8 bits remain). delta-index.c:581-596.

name: move_bits_down
prose: Precondition: size > MAX_BIG_FIELD_BITS (57); all bytes read by the field accesses are readable and all bytes written are writable, namely from + from_offset/8 up to at most 7 bytes beyond (from_offset + size)/8, and likewise for to; and either to_offset < from_offset or the source and destination bit ranges do not overlap. Postcondition: the size bits of to starting at bit to_offset equal the bits the source range held before the call and no bits outside the destination range change. It first moves one field that ends on a 32-bit boundary of the destination, then 32-bit chunks (reading 8 bytes and writing 4 bytes per step) from lower to higher addresses while more than 57 bits remain, then any remaining bits as a single field.
note: delta-index.c:598-636. Overlap analysis: with to_offset < from_offset the destination pointer never exceeds the source pointer, so writes do not clobber bytes still to be read. Only called from move_bits.

name: move_bits_up
prose: Precondition: size > MAX_BIG_FIELD_BITS (57); all bytes read by the field accesses are readable and all bytes written are writable (from + from_offset/8 up to at most 7 bytes beyond (from_offset + size)/8, likewise for to); and either from_offset <= to_offset or the ranges do not overlap. Postcondition: the size bits of to starting at bit to_offset equal the bits the source range held before the call and no bits outside the destination range change. It first moves the top (to_offset + size) % 32 bits as one field (if non-zero), then 32-bit chunks from higher to lower addresses while more than 57 bits remain, then the remaining low bits as a single field.
note: delta-index.c:638-674. Only called from move_bits when from_offset <= to_offset.

name: move_bits
prose: Precondition: the bytes read and written by the field accesses are valid, from + from_offset/8 up to at most 7 bytes beyond (from_offset + size)/8 for the source and likewise for the destination (nothing is accessed when size is 0). Postcondition: the size bits of to starting at bit to_offset equal the bits the source range held before the call, even when the ranges overlap, and no bits outside the destination range change. If size <= MAX_BIG_FIELD_BITS (57) it reads the whole field first and then writes it (nothing when size is 0); otherwise it calls move_bits_down when from_offset > to_offset and move_bits_up otherwise.
note: delta-index.c:676-694. Not stating MAX_BIG_FIELD_BITS in terms of a fixed access bound beyond the +7 byte window.

name: uds_pack_delta_index_page
prose: Precondition: delta_index is an initialized delta index whose zone 0 holds delta lists numbered up to list_count (list 0 of the zone array being the head guard, so lists first_list.. are at index first_list + 1), first_list <= delta_index->list_count, memory points to a writable page of memory_size bytes, and list_count points to a writable u32. Postcondition: if memory_size * 8 minus the header offset for one list and the guard bits is less than IMMUTABLE_HEADER_SIZE it logs an error and returns UDS_OVERFLOW, leaving *list_count and the page untouched. Otherwise it counts how many consecutive lists starting at first_list (at most delta_index->list_count - first_list) fit in the remaining bits, where each costs IMMUTABLE_HEADER_SIZE plus its size in bits (this count may be 0), stores that count in *list_count, writes the page header (nonce, virtual chapter number, first_list and the list count, the last two as 16-bit values), the offset table, the list data copied with move_bits, sets the last POST_FIELD_GUARD_BYTES of the page to 0xFF, and returns UDS_SUCCESS. Only delta zone 0 is read; delta_index is not modified.
note: Old prose claimed overflow only when the page cannot hold 'any' list; the code (delta-index.c:1345) checks free_bits < IMMUTABLE_HEADER_SIZE, and the loop can still pack 0 lists with success. Also first_list and n_lists are stored as le16 (truncation not guarded).

name: compute_new_list_offsets
prose: Precondition: delta_zone is initialized with list_count > 0 (it is a divisor), delta_zone->delta_lists has entries 0..list_count+1 (head guard, lists, tail guard), new_offsets has room for list_count + 2 entries, and used_space <= delta_zone->size (otherwise the unsigned subtraction wraps). Postcondition: only delta_zone->new_offsets is written. With spacing = (size - used_space) / list_count in bytes and byte offsets B[0] = 0, B[i+1] = B[i] + get_delta_list_byte_size(&delta_lists[i]) + spacing, where B[1] is reduced by spacing/2 and B[growing_index] is increased by growing_size (growing_size in bytes, and both adjustments carry into all later offsets), new_offsets[i] = B[i] * 8 + (delta_lists[i].start % 8) for 0 <= i <= list_count, and new_offsets[list_count + 1] = delta_zone->size * 8 - delta_lists[list_count + 1].size.
note: Old prose said new_offsets[0] was the head guard's bit offset; code gives new_offsets[0] = 0*8 + delta_lists[0].start % 8 (delta-index.c:1406-1412), i.e. only the intra-byte part. The adjustments are cumulative because later B values are built from earlier ones. growing_index of 0 never matches.

name: uds_radix_sort
prose: Precondition: sorter is a radix sorter from uds_make_radix_sorter, keys points to count pointers to keys that are each at least length bytes long. Postcondition: if count is 0 or length is 0 it returns UDS_SUCCESS without touching keys. If count <= INSERTION_SORT_THRESHOLD (12) it insertion-sorts the pointers by memcmp of the first length bytes and returns UDS_SUCCESS. If count > sorter->count it returns UDS_INVALID_ARGUMENT with keys unchanged. Otherwise it radix-sorts the pointer array (unstable) by the key bytes and returns UDS_SUCCESS with the pointers ordered by memcmp over the length bytes; if a sub-task push fails because the sorter's task stack is full (UDS_BAD_STATE from push_bins) it zeroes the histogram (memset of sorter->bins) and returns that error with the pointer array only partially sorted (still a permutation of the same pointers).
note: Packet name 'radix_sort' is not defined; real function is uds_radix_sort (radix-sort.c:230-330) -- slice cut the head. Old prose said the 'task stack and insertion list may be left partially consumed'; those are only local pointers into the sorter's scratch arrays, so removed. Contract empty: pointer args.

name: vdo_status_to_errno
prose: Precondition: error is any int. Postcondition: returns error unchanged if error <= 0; returns -error if 0 < error < 1024; for error >= 1024 it returns -ENOSPC when error is VDO_NO_SPACE and -EIO when error is VDO_READ_ONLY (neither logs); for any other value >= 1024 it logs an info message with the error's name and text via uds_string_error_name and uds_string_error and returns -EIO. It acquires no locks or references.
note: Old prose said any code >= 1024 other than NO_SPACE logs; VDO_READ_ONLY returns -EIO without logging (status-codes.c:1560-1561). Old contract used 1027 for VDO_NO_SPACE, which is not its value (it is in the VDO block starting at 1464); contract dropped because the function logs (global side effect) and relies on enum constants. Source line 66 in the packet is the comment tail; function at ~74.

name: writecache_map_write
prose: Precondition: the caller holds wc->lock (writecache_wait_on_freelist drops and retakes it, so state may change while waiting) and bio is a write bio. Postcondition: it processes the bio one cache block per loop pass until bi_size is 0 or it returns. (1) If writecache_has_error is true at the start of a pass it adds the remaining bio blocks to stats.writes and returns WC_MAP_ERROR without routing the bio (blocks copied in earlier passes, pmem mode only, stay in the cache). (2) If no cache entry exists for the sector and the target is in cleaner mode, or metadata_only is set and the bio lacks REQ_META, or there is no free entry, mode is not pmem and no existing entry was found, it remaps the bio towards the origin device (trimmed with dm_accept_partial_bio to the next cached entry), counts writes_around/writes and returns WC_MAP_REMAP_ORIGIN; this can happen in pmem mode too (cleaner/metadata_only). (3) If an entry exists and is uncommitted, or (non-pmem, committed, no write_in_progress) overwritable, it reuses that entry; otherwise it takes a free entry, waits on the freelist (and repeats the pass) when none is free in pmem mode or when an existing committed entry was found, then records the sector and sequence count, inserts the entry and increments uncommitted_blocks. (4) In pmem mode it copies the block data into pmem and continues with the next block; in SSD mode it calls writecache_bio_copy_ssd (which points the bio at the SSD cache sectors, possibly truncating it with dm_accept_partial_bio) and returns WC_MAP_REMAP. (5) After the pmem loop finishes, it flushes the cache if the bio has REQ_FUA or uncommitted_blocks >= autocommit_blocks, else schedules autocommit, and returns WC_MAP_SUBMIT.
note: Reviewers: (1) error path returns without routing: right, now stated. (2) non-pmem does not copy data: right; prose says SSD mode retargets. (3) pmem can return WC_MAP_REMAP_ORIGIN for cleaner/metadata_only: right (dm-writecache.c:1605-1607 goto direct_write), old prose attributed REMAP_ORIGIN to SSD mode only; fixed. In pmem mode with no free entry the code waits, never remaps (1611). Real function at line 1437 of the file.

name: dm_split_and_process_bio
prose: Precondition: md, map and bio are valid, map being the loaded table. Postcondition: returns no value; the bio is consumed by one of these paths. (1) If need_split (an abnormal bio, or with zoned support enabled dm_zone_bio_needs_split) it replaces bio by bio_split_to_limits(bio) and returns at once if that returns NULL. (2) With zoned support enabled, if dm_zone_plug_bio(md, bio) returns true it returns. (3) For a REQ_NOWAIT bio that is not abnormal: with REQ_PREFLUSH it calls bio_wouldblock_error and returns; otherwise it calls alloc_io(md, bio, GFP_NOWAIT) and if that fails calls bio_wouldblock_error and returns. All other bios use alloc_io(md, bio, GFP_NOIO), whose result is not checked. (4) After init_clone_info: a REQ_PREFLUSH bio goes to the data path only when it has data, map->flush_bypasses_map is set and the table's device list has exactly one entry; otherwise it sets io->requeue_flush_with_data if it has data, sends an empty flush with __send_empty_flush and goes to out. (5) On the data path a zoned REQ_OP_ZONE_RESET_ALL bio sets error from __send_zone_reset_all and goes to out; otherwise error is set from __split_and_process_bio, and if error is 0 and ci.sector_count is nonzero the remaining part is trimmed with bio_trim, traced, bio_inc_remaining(bio) is called and it is resubmitted with submit_bio_noacct. (6) At out, if error is nonzero or the clone info is not polled, it decrements io->io_count when error is nonzero and calls dm_io_dec_pending(io, error); otherwise it calls dm_queue_poll_io(bio, io).
note: Reviewer: 'says non-abnormal REQ_NOWAIT success allocates GFP_NOIO; code uses GFP_NOWAIT' -- right about the old wording; fixed (dm.c:1691-1709). Real source line 1948 of file.

name: md_bitmap_new_disk_sb
prose: Precondition: bitmap points to a struct bitmap with a valid mddev; bitmap->storage.sb_page is overwritten (a previously held page is not released); mddev->bitmap_info.chunksize must be nonzero (BUG_ON otherwise). Postcondition: allocates a zeroed page into bitmap->storage.sb_page and sets storage.sb_index to 0; returns -ENOMEM if the allocation fails (nothing is mapped). Otherwise it kmap_local_page-maps the page and writes magic and version; if chunksize is not a power of two it unmaps the page, warns and returns -EINVAL, leaving the allocated page in bitmap->storage.sb_page, with only magic and version written and no other bitmap or mddev field changed. Otherwise it writes chunksize, daemon_sleep (5*HZ if the configured value is 0 or above MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT; stored back to mddev->bitmap_info.daemon_sleep), write_behind (max_write_behind capped at COUNTER_MAX/2 and stored back to mddev->bitmap_info.max_write_behind), sync_size from mddev->resync_max_sectors, the uuid and, after setting BITMAP_STALE in bitmap->flags, state and events_cleared (bitmap->events_cleared is set to mddev->events), sets mddev->bitmap_info.nodes to 0, unmaps the page and returns 0. The page is unmapped on every path where it was mapped, but the allocated page itself remains owned by bitmap->storage.
note: Packet name 'md_bitmap_update_sb' does not exist in md-bitmap.c (there is bitmap_update_sb at line 680 with a different behavior); the described code is md_bitmap_new_disk_sb at line 759, slice cut the head. Old prose wrongly required sb_page to be valid on entry and said the caller keeps no reference; the function allocates the page and leaves it in bitmap->storage even in the -EINVAL case.

name: super_90_validate
prose: Precondition: rdev->sb_page holds a v0.90 superblock and rdev->desc_nr indexes a valid entry of its disks array; freshest is unused. Postcondition: it first sets rdev->raid_disk to -1 and clears the Faulty, In_sync, Bitmap_sync and WriteMostly flags. If mddev->raid_disks is 0 it copies the version, geometry, level, layout, event count, reshape fields, resync offset, uuid and bitmap defaults from the superblock into mddev. Else if mddev->pers is NULL it increments the event count and returns -EINVAL when the descriptor has MD_DISK_SYNC or MD_DISK_ACTIVE set and the count is below mddev->events. Else if mddev->bitmap exists it returns 0 without applying the descriptor when the event count is below md_bitmap_events_cleared(mddev), and sets Bitmap_sync when it is below mddev->events. Else it returns 0 without applying the descriptor when the event count is below mddev->events (a hot-add leaves raid_disk at -1). Otherwise, using the descriptor: Faulty is set if MD_DISK_FAULTY; else if MD_DISK_SYNC it sets In_sync and sets raid_disk and saved_raid_disk to desc->raid_disk; else if MD_DISK_ACTIVE and mddev->minor_version >= 91 it sets recovery_offset to 0 and raid_disk to desc->raid_disk. It then sets WriteMostly and FailFast from the descriptor flags and returns 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 (early returns skip descriptor updates, flags set only conditionally) is right; old prose said 'in every path'. Old -EINVAL condition omitted that mddev->raid_disks != 0 (md.c:1938). Real function at line 1474 of file.

name: slot_store
prose: Precondition: rdev and rdev->mddev are initialised and buf is a NUL-terminated string. Postcondition: returns -EBUSY if the Journal flag is set. If buf begins with "none" the slot is -1; otherwise buf is parsed with kstrtouint (base 10), returning its negative error on failure or -ENOSPC if the value does not fit in a positive int. If the array is active (mddev->pers non-NULL) and slot is -1: returns -EEXIST if rdev->raid_disk is -1, -EINVAL if the personality has no hot_remove_disk; otherwise it clears Blocked, calls remove_and_add_spares, returns -EBUSY if rdev->raid_disk is still >= 0, else sets MD_RECOVERY_NEEDED and returns len. If the array is active and slot >= 0: returns -EBUSY if rdev->raid_disk != -1 or MD_RECOVERY_RUNNING is set, -EINVAL if hot_add_disk is NULL, -ENOSPC if slot >= raid_disks and slot >= raid_disks + delta_disks; otherwise it sets raid_disk to slot, saved_raid_disk to slot if In_sync was set or -1 otherwise, clears In_sync and Bitmap_sync and calls hot_add_disk; on error it resets raid_disk to -1 and returns the error (saved_raid_disk and the cleared flags are left as modified); on success it notifies the sysfs state entry, calls sysfs_link_rdev ignoring its result and returns len. If the array is inactive: returns -ENOSPC under the same slot bound, otherwise sets raid_disk to slot (-1 for "none"), clears Faulty and WriteMostly, sets In_sync, notifies the sysfs state entry and returns len.
note: Reviewers: (1) slot bound / missing -EINVAL for NULL hot_add_disk -- already in the old prose (md.c:2040-2045). (2) 'actual returns hot_remove_disk error' -- wrong: hot_remove_disk is only checked for NULL and the code returns -EBUSY when raid_disk >= 0 after remove_and_add_spares (2018-2026). Added the inactive 'none' behavior and the hot_add error side effects. Real source line 3277.

name: md_set_readonly
prose: Precondition: mddev->pers is non-NULL and the caller holds mddev->reconfig_mutex (stop_sync_thread(mddev, false) releases it, and the function takes it again with mddev_lock_nointr). Postcondition: if mddev->external and MD_SB_CHANGE_PENDING is set it returns -EBUSY at once with no state change and the lock still held. Otherwise it sets MD_RECOVERY_FROZEN if it was clear (did_freeze), stops the sync thread (which drops the mutex), waits until MD_SB_CHANGE_PENDING is clear, and retakes the mutex. If MD_RECOVERY_RUNNING is then set it warns and goes to out with -EBUSY without calling __md_stop_writes. Otherwise it calls __md_stop_writes; if mddev->ro is already MD_RDONLY it goes to out with -ENXIO (the writes were already stopped), else it sets mddev->ro to MD_RDONLY, marks the gendisk read-only and falls through to out with 0. At out, if the result is 0 or did_freeze is set it clears MD_RECOVERY_FROZEN (even if it was set on entry when the result is 0), sets MD_RECOVERY_NEEDED and notifies mddev->sysfs_state; otherwise those are left alone. It returns with mddev->reconfig_mutex held on every path after the early -EBUSY (which also leaves it held); it does not release it.
note: Reviewers: (1) -ENXIO path already ran __md_stop_writes: right and now stated (md.c:2109-2114). (2) on success with FROZEN already set it is cleared: right (2120-2121), stated. (3) 'code does not release reconfig_mutex before returning': right; old prose wrongly claimed the mutex is released. Also old precondition ('caller does not hold the mutex') was wrong: stop_sync_thread(mddev, false) unlocks it (md.c:5175-5183) so the caller must hold it. Callers at 4712, 4722, 8310 are in locked context. Real source line 6983.

name: mddev_alloc_unit
prose: Precondition: the caller holds all_mddevs_lock (mddev_find_locked scans the all_mddevs list and the function takes no lock itself). Postcondition: uses and updates the static next_minor (initially 512). Starting with start = next_minor, each pass builds dev = MKDEV(MD_MAJOR, next_minor), increments next_minor (wrapping to 0 after MINORMASK) and then, if next_minor has come back to start, returns 0 without testing that pass's dev; otherwise it returns dev when mddev_find_locked(dev) finds no mddev with that unit. Hence on a nonzero return the minor is the value next_minor had at the start of the successful pass (not necessarily the entry value), next_minor is that minor + 1 modulo MINORMASK + 1, and no mddev on the list has that unit. On a 0 return the MINORMASK candidates start, start+1, ... (mod MINORMASK + 1) were all found in use, the last candidate (start - 1 mod MINORMASK + 1) was never tested, and next_minor is back to its entry value. It allocates and frees nothing and does not change the lock state.
note: Reviewer round 15 ('code tests all MINORMASK+1 including start-1') is wrong: md.c:2149-2150 returns 0 as soon as next_minor == start, before mddev_find_locked is called for the candidate built in that pass, so start-1 is untested. Reviewer round 2 (minor need not equal entry next_minor; 0 without testing last minor) is right and the old prose already says this. Contract left empty: static state and list scan.

name: raid1_sync_request
prose: Precondition: mddev is an initialised raid1 array with conf == mddev->private, called from the resync/recovery thread with sector_nr the next sector to sync and max_sector the end of the range; skipped points to an int that the caller reads afterwards. Postcondition: returns 0 without setting *skipped if the r1buf pool is not initialised and init_resync fails, or, at the end (sector_nr >= max_sector), after calling md_bitmap_end_sync when the sync was aborted (curr_resync < max_sector) or else clearing conf->fullsync, closing the bitmap sync when enabled, close_sync(conf), and clearing the cluster window when clustered; or if raise_barrier fails (it returns -EINTR when MD_RECOVERY_INTR is set), in which case no r1bio has been allocated. It sets *skipped to 1 and returns max_sector - sector_nr when there is no bitmap, resync_offset is MaxSector, MD_RECOVERY_REQUESTED is clear and conf->fullsync is 0, and sets *skipped to 1 and returns sync_blocks when md_bitmap_start_sync(.., true) says nothing needs syncing and neither fullsync nor MD_RECOVERY_REQUESTED applies. Otherwise it may sleep one tick if regular I/O is waiting, calls the bitmap cond_end_sync, raises the barrier, allocates an r1bio and classifies each mirror: absent or Faulty devices are skipped, devices not In_sync become write targets, In_sync devices without bad blocks at this range become read targets, and an In_sync device with bad blocks at the start becomes a write target only when MD_RECOVERY_SYNC is set, MD_RECOVERY_CHECK is clear and WriteErrorSeen is clear. An nr_pending reference is taken on every device that gets a bio. If there are no read targets and min_bad > 0 it records the bad range on every write target, sets MD_SB_CHANGE_DEVS, sets *skipped to 1 and releases the r1bio with put_buf (dropping the references and lowering the barrier); it then returns min_bad, or, if rdev_set_badblocks failed on any target, sets conf->recovery_disabled and MD_RECOVERY_INTR and returns 0. Else, if there are no write targets or no read targets, it sets *skipped to 1, calls put_buf and returns max_sector - sector_nr (with max_sector first set to sector_nr + min_bad when min_bad > 0). Otherwise it limits the range by mddev->resync_max and good_sectors, adds resync pages to every bio with a bi_end_io (stopping early if the bitmap says the range need not be synced and neither fullsync nor MD_RECOVERY_REQUESTED applies), updates the cluster resync window when clustered, submits the read bio(s) (all read targets when MD_RECOVERY_REQUESTED, else only the read_disk bio; completion is handled by the end_sync_* handlers) and returns nr_sectors, the number of sectors added to the bios (possibly 0).
note: Reviewer round 15 ('no pre-check md_bitmap_start_sync sets *skipped and returns sync_blocks; that check is inside the do-loop') is wrong: the pre-check exists at raid1.c:2219-2224 (source dump) and does set *skipped = 1 and return sync_blocks; a second md_bitmap_start_sync call inside the loop (line ~2395 of dump) only breaks the loop. Added the raise_barrier -EINTR cause and target-classification detail. Real source line 2749.

name: raid10_handle_discard
prose: Precondition: mddev is a raid10 array with mddev->private a valid r10conf and bio is a discard bio for which the caller (raid10_make_request) has already called md_write_start. Postcondition: if MD_RECOVERY_RESHAPE is set on entry it returns -EAGAIN at once without waiting for the barrier and without touching the bio. Otherwise it calls wait_barrier; if MD_RECOVERY_RESHAPE is now set or the bio is smaller than twice the stripe size it calls allow_barrier and returns -EAGAIN, with the bio unmodified. Otherwise it splits off an unaligned head (and, separately, an unaligned tail) at stripe_size boundaries with bio_split, chains the pieces to the bio, drops the barrier, resubmits the head part (or the tail, in the second case) with submit_bio_noacct and takes the barrier again; if either bio_split fails it sets the bio's status from the error, calls bio_endio(bio), md_write_end(mddev), allow_barrier and returns 0. Then, for each far copy (once, or conf->geo.far_copies times when geo->far_offset is 0), it allocates an r10bio, calls wait_blocked_dev, takes an nr_pending reference on every non-Faulty rdev and replacement of each member disk, computes the per-disk discard range [dev_start, dev_end), and for each such device clones the bio, sets raid10_end_discard_request as its completion handler, increments r10_bio->remaining, calls md_submit_discard_bio for the range and calls bio_endio on the clone. Between far copies it calls raid_end_discard_bio on the finished r10bio and wait_barrier again. Finally it calls raid_end_discard_bio on the last r10bio and returns 0; raid_end_discard_bio releases the barrier (allow_barrier) each time an r10bio's remaining count reaches zero and, for the first r10bio, calls md_write_end, bio_endio on the master bio and frees it. The nr_pending references are dropped later by raid10_end_discard_request.
note: Packet name raid10_discard_request does not exist; the real function is raid10_handle_discard (raid10.c:1568), slice cut the head. Old prose said raid_end_discard_bio drops the nr_pending references; it does not (raid10_end_discard_request calls rdev_dec_pending, 1559). Old prose 'submits a cloned discard' is via md_submit_discard_bio + bio_endio(clone) (1793-1796). Non-far_offset layouts loop once per far copy (1814-1823).

name: raid10_sync_request
prose: Precondition: mddev is a raid10 array with an initialised conf, sector_nr is the next virtual sector to sync, max_sector the end of the range, and skipped points to an int the caller reads afterwards. Postcondition: returns, with *skipped set as stated: (1) mddev->dev_sectors - sector_nr with *skipped = 1 when there is no bitmap, resync_offset and reshape_position are MaxSector, none of MD_RECOVERY_SYNC, MD_RECOVERY_REQUESTED, MD_RECOVERY_RESHAPE is set and conf->fullsync is 0; (2) 0 when the r10buf pool is uninitialised and init_resync fails; (3) at or beyond the end (sector_nr >= max_sector, tested at the start and again after each skipped chunk) it clears the cluster window and, if MD_RECOVERY_RESHAPE is set, calls end_reshape and close_sync and returns 0 without touching *skipped, otherwise it ends the bitmap sync for an aborted run or (completed run) marks replacements recovered when a full sync completed and clears conf->fullsync, closes the bitmap sync and close_sync, sets *skipped = 1 and returns sectors_skipped; (4) reshape_request(mddev, sector_nr, skipped)'s value when MD_RECOVERY_RESHAPE is set; (5) after chunks_skipped reaches raid_disks it logs an error and either, for recovery with error_disk >= 0, sets that mirror's recovery_disabled and returns 0, or sets *skipped = 1 and returns (max_sector - sector_nr) + sectors_skipped; (6) for resync, *skipped = 1 and sync_blocks + sectors_skipped when the bitmap says the block need not be synced (no fullsync, no MD_RECOVERY_REQUESTED); (7) otherwise, after limiting the range (resync_max, chunk boundary) and sleeping one tick when conf->nr_waiting is nonzero, it builds the list of read/write bios (recovery: per non-in-sync or replaced device, reading from an In_sync copy; resync: reading every readable copy and writing replacements), raising the barrier and taking nr_pending references, adds resync pages, submits only the read bios (writes are issued from the read completion), calls md_done_sync(mddev, sectors_skipped, 1) if some sectors were skipped, and returns sectors_skipped + nr_sectors. If no bio could be built (recovery with an empty list, or resync with fewer than two targets) or bio_add_page fails it takes the giveup path: it advances sector_nr to the end of the current range, adds that to sectors_skipped, increments chunks_skipped and re-enters at the skipped label. For recovery with no usable source for a device it may record bad blocks and, if that fails or none worked, sets MD_RECOVERY_INTR and mirror->recovery_disabled, releasing that r10bio and its references.
note: Reviewer round 15 (skip path returns sync_blocks + sectors_skipped, not dev_sectors - sector_nr) is partly right: both exist (raid10.c:3130+ clean-array skip at the top, and resync skip at 3538-3545 of the dump numbering); old prose omitted the sync_blocks + sectors_skipped one. Old claim 'on every path either hands the queued bios to the block layer or releases the barrier and buffers' is not supported: the bio_add_page failure path (3654-3658) ends the bio and goes to giveup, and recovery's biolist path does not mention it; removed. Real source line 3130 of file; slice cut the head.

name: reshape_request
prose: Precondition: mddev is a raid10 array in the middle of a reshape with conf->reshape_progress and reshape_safe set, called from the recovery thread (which holds no barrier of its own). Postcondition: returns the number of sectors for which read bios were submitted. (1) If sector_nr is 0 and conf->reshape_progress shows a restart point (backwards: reshape_progress < array size, so sector_nr = size - reshape_progress; forwards: reshape_progress > 0, so sector_nr = reshape_progress) it sets mddev->curr_resync_completed to it, notifies the sysfs completed entry, sets *skipped = 1 and returns that position without any I/O. (2) Otherwise it computes the window and, if the new write position may pass the safe position (need_flush) or the last checkpoint is more than 10*HZ old, it calls wait_barrier, writes reshape_position and curr_resync_completed, sets MD_SB_CHANGE_DEVS, wakes the md thread and waits for sb_flags to clear or MD_RECOVERY_INTR; if MD_RECOVERY_INTR is set it calls allow_barrier and returns 0, else it sets conf->reshape_safe and calls allow_barrier. (3) It then raises the barrier and loops: allocate an r10bio (raise_barrier again), read_balance for a readable device; if none, it frees the r10bio, sets MD_RECOVERY_INTR and returns the sectors done so far with the barrier still raised and reshape_progress unchanged; otherwise it builds the read bio and the write bios for each non-Faulty rdev and replacement (end_reshape_write), adds pages to all of them, and if a bio_add_page fails ends that bio with BLK_STS_RESOURCE and returns the sectors done so far (barrier still raised, reshape_progress unchanged). Only the read bio is submitted here (submit_bio_noacct); the write bios are submitted after the read completes. (4) When the whole window has been queued it calls lower_barrier, advances conf->reshape_progress by sectors_done (subtracts it when reshaping backwards) and returns sectors_done.
note: Reviewer round 15 'does not submit per-copy writes; only the read is submitted' is right (raid10.c:4849-4853 submits read_bio only); old prose said it submits the read and the per-copy writes. This is the raid10.c function, distinct from the raid5.c reshape_request of record 24. Real source line 4597. Early INTR return returns sectors_done == 0 at that point.

name: handle_stripe
prose: Precondition: sh is a valid stripe_head for which the caller holds a reference, with sh->raid_conf pointing to the array's r5conf. Postcondition: returns no value. STRIPE_HANDLE is cleared at entry, but this function (or the helpers it calls) may set it again, so it is not guaranteed clear on return. (1) If clear_batch_ready(sh) returns nonzero (sh is a non-head member of a batch) it returns at once; that call has already cleared STRIPE_BATCH_READY on sh, so STRIPE_HANDLE and STRIPE_BATCH_READY are clear and no other state is changed here. (2) Otherwise, if STRIPE_ACTIVE was already set it sets STRIPE_HANDLE and returns, leaving STRIPE_ACTIVE set. (3) Otherwise it owns STRIPE_ACTIVE: it clears STRIPE_BATCH_ERR and, if it was set, calls break_stripe_batch_list(sh, 0); if STRIPE_SYNC_REQUESTED is set and sh->batch_head is NULL it takes sh->stripe_lock and, only if STRIPE_R5C_PARTIAL_STRIPE, STRIPE_R5C_FULL_STRIPE and STRIPE_DISCARD are all clear, converts STRIPE_SYNC_REQUESTED into STRIPE_SYNCING and clears STRIPE_INSYNC and STRIPE_REPLACED; it clears STRIPE_DELAYED and runs analyse_stripe. It jumps straight to the finish label if STRIPE_LOG_TRAPPED is set, or (after setting STRIPE_HANDLE) if s.handle_bad_blocks is set or the array is read/write with MD_SB_CHANGE_PENDING set, or (after setting STRIPE_HANDLE) if s.blocked_rdev is non-NULL and any of s.syncing, s.expanding, s.expanded, s.replacing, s.to_write, s.written is set; with s.blocked_rdev non-NULL and none of those set it drops that rdev's pending reference and clears s.blocked_rdev. Otherwise it proceeds through the normal stripe-handling steps (failed-stripe handling when more devices failed than max_degraded, completion of write reconstruction, clean-event handling, fills, dirtying, parity checks, replacement writes, sync completion, read-error repair and expansion handling), and some of those steps may also jump to finish (handle_stripe_dirtying returning -EAGAIN, or an expand-source stripe not yet read). At finish it releases or waits on s.blocked_rdev (md_wait_for_blocked_rdev when mddev->external, else rdev_dec_pending), applies pending R5_WriteError, R5_MadeGood and R5_MadeGoodRepl bad-block updates when s.handle_bad_blocks is set (dropping the rdev references), calls raid_run_ops if ops were requested, calls ops_run_io, decrements conf->preread_active_stripes when s.dec_preread_active is set (waking the md thread when it falls below IO_THRESHOLD), and finally clears STRIPE_ACTIVE with clear_bit_unlock.
note: Reviewers: (1) HANDLE not guaranteed cleared: right, already stated (retry/blocked paths set it). (2) 'precondition excludes non-head batch members': wrong for current prose, which includes the batch-member early return (raid5.c:5000s clear_batch_ready, source dump 3208-3209). (3) clear_batch_ready can clear STRIPE_BATCH_READY on the early return, so 'no other change' is false: right (raid5.c:4820 test_and_clear_bit); fixed. Real function at line 4913 of the dump numbering.

name: reshape_request
prose: Precondition: mddev->private is a valid r5conf in the middle of a reshape, sector_nr is the current reshape position in sectors (0 on the first call), skipped is a valid pointer, and the caller holds neither conf->device_lock nor stripe references that this function needs. Postcondition: it returns MaxSector without further effects if a WARN_ON consistency check fails (backwards: writepos < reshape_sectors, or reshape_progress == 0, or the computed stripe_addr does not match sector_nr; forwards: writepos != sector_nr + reshape_sectors). If sector_nr is 0 and a restart position gives a non-zero sector_nr (reshape_progress converted per new data disk; backwards with reshape_progress == MaxSector gives MaxSector) it sets curr_resync_completed, notifies the sysfs completed entry, sets *skipped = 1, sets the return value to that skipped count and goes to the finish step. Otherwise, if the superblock must be updated (the safe position lags and the read position is past the write position, or the checkpoint is older than 10*HZ), it waits for conf->reshape_stripes to drop to 0 or MD_RECOVERY_INTR, returning 0 if reshape_stripes is still non-zero, updates reshape_position, curr_resync_completed and (forwards) the recovery_offset of non-in-sync rdevs, sets MD_SB_CHANGE_DEVS and waits for it to clear, returning 0 if MD_RECOVERY_INTR is set, else updates conf->reshape_safe under device_lock. It then takes reshape_sectors = max(chunk_sectors, prev_chunk_sectors) worth of destination stripes with raid5_get_active_stripe, sets STRIPE_EXPANDING on each and increments reshape_stripes, zeroes (and marks R5_Expanded and R5_UPTODATE) every data block lying beyond the end of the old array, and sets STRIPE_EXPAND_READY and STRIPE_HANDLE on a destination stripe only when none of its data blocks lies inside the old array; it advances conf->reshape_progress by reshape_sectors * new_data_disks in the reshape direction under device_lock, marks the mapped source stripes STRIPE_EXPAND_SOURCE and STRIPE_HANDLE, releases every stripe reference it took, and sets the return value to reshape_sectors. At the finish step, if curr_resync_completed is beyond resync_max or the progress has reached half of the remaining distance to resync_max, it waits for reshape_stripes to reach 0 or MD_RECOVERY_INTR and, if that holds, does the same superblock update and wait; whether it succeeds or is interrupted at this point it returns the value already set (reshape_sectors or the skipped count), not 0. It leaves conf->device_lock unlocked.
note: Reviewer round 15 (finish path returns retn when MD_RECOVERY_INTR during the final superblock wait) is right (raid5.c:6489-6490, 6507-6508 goto ret returns retn); old prose said 0. Also old prose had EXPAND_READY backwards ('no disk lies beyond the old array'): skipped_disk is set when a data block is inside the old array (6425-6428) so the flags are set only when every data block is beyond it. Real source line 6242 of file; slice cut the head.

name: cec_config_thread_func
prose: Precondition: arg is a struct cec_adapter that is being configured (adap->is_configuring set) with log_addrs prepared; the caller (the config kthread) does not hold adap->lock, the function takes it itself. Postcondition: it returns 0 at both of its exits (configured and unconfigure) and ends with adap->lock released (the lock may be dropped and retaken inside cec_config_log_addr while a blocking poll is transmitted). It clears log_addr_mask. If the first log address type is CEC_LOG_ADDR_TYPE_UNREGISTERED it goes straight to the configured step. Otherwise, for each logical address i it picks the preferred list for the type (the TV type uses the Specific list when phys_addr is non-zero), tries the previous address (or the first in the list) with cec_config_log_addr, and: if adap->must_reconfigure is set after that first attempt it clears it, resets log_addr_mask and restarts the loop from i = 0; if the attempt claimed the address it continues; if it returned a negative error it goes to unconfigure; otherwise it tries the other addresses of the list (skipping the one already tried and, below CEC 2.0, the backup addresses), and a negative error from any of those goes to unconfigure (including the -EINTR that cec_config_log_addr returns when phys_addr became invalid or must_reconfigure was set during polling, so must_reconfigure does not restart the loop at that point). If afterwards no address was claimed and CEC_LOG_ADDRS_FL_ALLOW_UNREG_FALLBACK is not set it goes to unconfigure. Configured step: if log_addr_mask is 0 it falls back to the Unregistered address (log_addr[0] = UNREGISTERED, the others INVALID); entries beyond num_log_addrs are set to INVALID; it sets is_configured true and is_configuring and must_reconfigure false, posts a state event, and for each valid log address (none when CEC_LOG_ADDRS_FL_CDC_ONLY is set) queues, with non-blocking transmits, Report Features (only for non-Unregistered addresses at CEC 2.0 or later), Report Physical Address and, if vendor_id is not CEC_VENDOR_ID_NONE, Device Vendor ID; then it clears adap->kthread_config, completes adap->config_completion, unlocks adap->lock, calls the adapter's configured callback and returns 0. Unconfigure step: it sets all log_addr entries to CEC_LOG_ADDR_INVALID, calls cec_adap_unconfigure (clears log_addr_mask, is_configured false, flushes the transmit queue, wakes the kthread wait queue, posts a state event and calls the unconfigured op), sets is_configuring and must_reconfigure false, clears adap->kthread_config, completes adap->config_completion, unlocks adap->lock and returns 0 without calling the configured callback.

Old precondition fix (lock not held by caller) already correct. The function is at line 1400 of the file.

name: cec_transmit_msg_fh
prose: Precondition: the caller holds adap->lock; adap is valid, msg points to a valid cec_msg, fh is NULL or a valid cec_fh, and block says whether to wait for completion. Postcondition: it returns -ENODEV, without modifying *msg, if adap->devnode.unregistered is set. Otherwise it first resets msg->rx_ts, tx_ts, rx_status, tx_status, tx_arb_lost_cnt, tx_nack_cnt, tx_low_drive_cnt, tx_error_cnt and sequence to 0, masks msg->flags down to CEC_MSG_FL_REPLY_TO_FOLLOWERS, CEC_MSG_FL_RAW and (only when the message is a <Vendor Command With ID> with the reply-vendor-id flag) CEC_MSG_FL_REPLY_VENDOR_ID, sets msg->timeout to 1000 if a reply is requested and the timeout is 0, and clears CEC_MSG_FL_REPLY_TO_FOLLOWERS if the timeout is 0. It then returns -EINVAL if msg->len is 0 or above CEC_MAX_MSG_SIZE or if a vendor-id reply is wanted and msg->len < 6; it zero-pads msg->msg beyond msg->len; and returns -EINVAL if msg->timeout is nonzero and msg->len is 1. For a raw message it returns -EPERM unless the caller has CAP_SYS_RAWIO. For a non-raw message it returns -EINVAL for a non-CDC message sent by a CDC-only adapter, writes the physical address into msg->msg[2..3] of a CDC message of length >= 4, returns -EINVAL for a poll (len 1) to destination 0xf, and for a poll to a logical address the adapter has itself claimed returns 0 at once with tx_ts set, tx_status = CEC_TX_STATUS_NACK | CEC_TX_STATUS_MAX_RETRIES, tx_nack_cnt = 1 and a nonzero sequence, queueing nothing; it returns -EINVAL for a non-broadcast message longer than 1 byte addressed to a claimed address, or (for len > 1) when the adapter is configured and the initiator is not a claimed address, and -ENONET when the adapter is unconfigured and not configuring unless the message is a Ping or IMAGE_VIEW_ON/TEXT_VIEW_ON to the TV. For any message (raw or not), when the adapter is unconfigured and not configuring, it returns -ENONET if needs_hpd is set and -EINVAL if a reply (or vendor-id reply) is requested. It returns -EBUSY when transmit_queue_sz has reached CEC_MAX_MSG_TX_QUEUE_SZ and -ENOMEM if the cec_data allocation fails. Otherwise it sets a nonzero msg->sequence, copies *msg into the new cec_data, links it into adap->transmit_queue (and fh->xfer_list when fh is non-NULL), increments transmit_queue_sz, wakes the kthread if nothing is transmitting and, if block is false, returns 0 with the data queued. If block is true it unlocks adap->lock, waits killably for completion, cancels the delayed work, relocks adap->lock, sets transmit_in_progress_aborted if the wait failed, cancels the transmit if it had not completed, copies the final data->msg back into *msg, removes and frees the data and returns 0 even if the wait was interrupted. On every return the caller again holds adap->lock.
note: Reviewers: (1) validation failures modify msg: right, stated. (2) -ENODEV returns before any modification: right, stated (cec-adap.c:3903-3904 in dump). (3) -EINVAL for unconfigured reply with needs_hpd false applies to raw messages too: right (code at 4021-4032 is outside the is_raw branch); old prose had restricted it to non-raw; fixed. Also added the CDC phys-addr write into msg->msg. Real source line 774.

name: cec_transmit_msg
prose: Precondition: adap is a valid CEC adapter, msg points to a valid cec_msg, and the caller does not already hold adap->lock. Postcondition: it takes adap->lock, calls cec_transmit_msg_fh(adap, msg, NULL, block), releases adap->lock and returns that call's value unchanged, so the lock is not held on return (cec_transmit_msg_fh itself drops and retakes it while waiting when block is true). The returned value is 0 (including a self-poll NACK result, a queued non-blocking message, and a completed or interrupted blocking transmit) or one of -ENODEV, -EINVAL, -EPERM, -ENONET, -EBUSY, -ENOMEM from cec_transmit_msg_fh; this wrapper does not interpret msg->flags itself, and what it leaves in *msg is determined by cec_transmit_msg_fh.
note: Reviewers: lock released during blocking wait inside the callee: stated. 'does not clear reply_vendor_id/is_raw': right, the wrapper does not touch them; callee derives them. Old prose duplicated the callee's full error list; shortened to the set of errnos actually reachable (cec-adap.c:992-1000, callee 774+). Real source line 992.

name: cec_pin_tx_states
prose: Precondition: pin is a valid cec_pin whose state is one of the transmit states and ts is the current timestamp; the function drives the line through cec_pin_high/cec_pin_low and may wake pin->kthread_waitq. Postcondition: depending on pin->state: TX_WAIT_FOR_HIGH goes to idle (cec_pin_to_idle) if the line reads high, otherwise no change. TX_START_BIT_LOW moves to TX_START_BIT_HIGH (or the _SHORT or _LONG variant when the tx_short_start or tx_long_start error injection fires) and drives the line high; TX_START_BIT_LOW_CUSTOM moves to TX_START_BIT_HIGH_CUSTOM and drives it high. In TX_DATA_BIT_1_HIGH_POST_SAMPLE (and _SHORT/_LONG), if tx_nacked is set it calls cec_pin_to_idle, clears tx_msg.len and records work_tx_ts = ts and work_tx_status = CEC_TX_STATUS_NACK and wakes the kthread queue (the later tx_generated_poll test cannot hold because cec_pin_to_idle has just cleared tx_generated_poll); otherwise it continues as for the data-bit-high states. In the TX_DATA_BIT_{0,1}_HIGH states (including the SHORT/LONG variants), if the line reads low and tx_generated_poll is false it clears tx_msg.len, sets TX_WAIT_FOR_HIGH, records CEC_TX_STATUS_LOW_DRIVE with work_tx_ts = ts, increments tx_low_drive_cnt and wakes the queue; otherwise it continues as for TX_DATA_BIT_HIGH_CUSTOM: if tx_last_bit fires it goes idle, clears tx_msg.len and records CEC_TX_STATUS_OK and wakes the queue; else it increments tx_bit and continues as for the start-bit-high states. In those states, if tx_low_drive fires it drives the line low, sets TX_LOW_DRIVE, clears tx_msg.len and, when tx_generated_poll is false, records CEC_TX_STATUS_LOW_DRIVE, increments tx_low_drive_cnt and wakes the queue; otherwise if tx_bit / 10 >= tx_msg.len + tx_extra_bytes it goes idle, clears tx_msg.len, records CEC_TX_STATUS_OK and wakes the queue; otherwise it picks the next bit (a data bit from tx_msg.msg or, for extra bytes, the byte index; the EOM bit from tx_post_eom and the last-byte position with the early-EOM and no-EOM injections; the ACK bit always as 1), sets TX_DATA_BIT_1_LOW or TX_DATA_BIT_0_LOW (TX_DATA_BIT_LOW_CUSTOM if tx_custom_bit fires) and drives the line low. TX_DATA_BIT_0_LOW and _1_LOW move to the matching high state (TX_DATA_BIT_1_HIGH_PRE_SAMPLE for a 1 in the first four bits or in the ACK bit, the SHORT/LONG variants when tx_short_bit or tx_long_bit fires outside the ACK bit) and drive the line high; TX_DATA_BIT_LOW_CUSTOM moves to TX_DATA_BIT_HIGH_CUSTOM and drives it high. In TX_DATA_BIT_1_HIGH_PRE_SAMPLE the line is sampled: if it reads low outside the ACK bit and tx_generated_poll is false, arbitration is lost, tx_msg.len is cleared, CEC_TX_STATUS_ARB_LOST is recorded, the queue woken, rx_bit is set to tx_bit, tx_bit to 0, rx_msg is zeroed and seeded with the masked first byte of tx_msg, rx_msg.len set to 0, pin->ts set to ts minus CEC_TIM_DATA_BIT_SAMPLE microseconds, state set to RX_DATA_POST_SAMPLE and rx_bit incremented; otherwise the state becomes TX_DATA_BIT_1_HIGH_POST_SAMPLE (or its SHORT/LONG variant under error injection outside the ACK bit) and, in the ACK bit, tx_nacked is set if the message was not acknowledged (broadcast: line low means NACK) and either tx_ignore_nack_until_eom is clear or this is the last byte, and tx_post_eom is false. TX_PULSE_LOW_CUSTOM drives the line high and moves to TX_PULSE_HIGH_CUSTOM; TX_PULSE_HIGH_CUSTOM goes idle; any other state is left unchanged.
note: Reviewer round 15 (tx_nacked path sets TX_WAIT_FOR_HIGH, not idle) is wrong: cec-pin.c:4196-4204 (dump) calls cec_pin_to_idle in that case; TX_WAIT_FOR_HIGH is set only in the low-line branch at 4227. Found: cec_pin_to_idle (cec-pin.c:351-370) clears tx_generated_poll, so the 'if (pin->tx_generated_poll) break;' tests that follow cec_pin_to_idle (NACK, last-bit, length-reached branches) never fire; old prose 'unless tx_generated_poll is set' for those cases was misleading and is corrected. Real source line 398 of the file.

name: cec_pin_rx_states
prose: Precondition: pin is a valid cec_pin whose state is one of the receive states and ts is the current timestamp; the function may drive the line and wake pin->kthread_waitq. Postcondition: depending on pin->state: RX_START_BIT_LOW reads the line; if it is still low nothing changes; otherwise the state becomes RX_START_BIT_HIGH, then if the low time is below CEC_TIM_START_BIT_LOW_MIN - CEC_TIM_IDLE_SAMPLE it increments rx_start_bit_low_too_short_cnt (storing the timestamp and delta on the first occurrence) and goes idle; else if the rx_arb_lost injection fires it initializes tx_msg from the poll byte, sets tx_generated_poll, sets tx_extra_bytes to 0, sets the state to TX_START_BIT_HIGH and pin->ts to ts. RX_START_BIT_HIGH: if the line is high and the time exceeds CEC_TIM_START_BIT_TOTAL_LONG it increments rx_start_bit_too_long_cnt (no timestamp recorded) and goes idle; if still high otherwise nothing changes; if low and the total time is below CEC_TIM_START_BIT_TOTAL_MIN - CEC_TIM_IDLE_SAMPLE it increments rx_start_bit_too_short_cnt (recording timestamp and delta on the first occurrence) and goes idle; else if the rx_low_drive injection fires it drives the line low, sets RX_LOW_DRIVE and increments rx_low_drive_cnt; else the state becomes RX_DATA_SAMPLE with pin->ts = ts and rx_eom false. RX_DATA_SAMPLE reads the line and sets RX_DATA_POST_SAMPLE; for bit positions other than 8 and 9 within a byte it ORs the value into rx_msg.msg[rx_bit/10] when rx_bit/10 < CEC_MAX_MSG_SIZE; at the EOM position (rx_bit % 10 == 8) it sets rx_eom and rx_msg.len to rx_bit/10 + 1; the ACK position (9) is not stored; it then increments rx_bit. RX_DATA_POST_SAMPLE sets RX_DATA_WAIT_FOR_LOW. RX_DATA_WAIT_FOR_LOW: if the line is high and the time exceeds CEC_TIM_DATA_BIT_TOTAL_LONG it increments rx_data_bit_too_long_cnt and goes idle; if still high nothing changes; if low and the rx_low_drive injection fires it drives the line low, sets RX_LOW_DRIVE and increments rx_low_drive_cnt; else if the bit time is below CEC_TIM_DATA_BIT_TOTAL_MIN and rx_no_low_drive is false it increments rx_data_bit_too_short_cnt (recording timestamp and delta on the first occurrence), drives the line low, sets RX_LOW_DRIVE and increments rx_low_drive_cnt; otherwise it sets pin->ts = ts and, if rx_bit % 10 != 9, goes to RX_DATA_SAMPLE; at the ACK position it decodes the destination from rx_msg, computes for_us (broadcast or in la_mask) and the ACK value (1 for broadcast, else !for_us, toggled when for_us and the rx_nack injection fires), and goes to RX_ACK_HIGH_POST if the value is 1, else drives the line low and goes to RX_ACK_LOW. RX_ACK_LOW drives the line high and goes to RX_ACK_LOW_POST. In RX_ACK_LOW_POST and RX_ACK_HIGH_POST, if the line reads high and rx_eom is set it copies rx_msg to work_rx_msg with rx_ts = ktime_to_ns(ts), wakes the queue, sets pin->ts = ts and goes to RX_ACK_FINISH; otherwise it increments rx_bit and goes to RX_DATA_WAIT_FOR_LOW. RX_ACK_FINISH goes idle. Any other state is left unchanged.
note: Reviewers: (1) too-long start bit increments counter without recording timestamp: right and already reflected (cec-pin.c RX_START_BIT_HIGH, dump 4463-4467). (2) RX_START_BIT_LOW sets RX_START_BIT_HIGH rather than leaving state unchanged when line is high: right and stated (dump 4436). (3) 'EOM check is rx_bit%10==8 not 9': partly right: the EOM bit is position 8 (EOM_BIT 8, ACK_BIT 9, cec-pin.c:63-64) and the prose now says so; the 'rx_bit % 10 != 9' test in WAIT_FOR_LOW is the ACK position test, which was correct. Real source line 665 of the file.

name: __prepare_userptr
prose: Precondition: vb is a valid vb2_buffer whose queue supports USERPTR, vb->num_planes <= VB2_MAX_PLANES, and the buf_ops fill_vb2_buffer callback converts the userspace plane description into a vb2_plane array. Postcondition: it records reacquired = (vb->planes[0].mem_priv == NULL) at entry. It first calls fill_vb2_buffer into a local planes[] array and returns its error immediately if non-zero, with no cleanup. For each plane whose stored m.userptr is zero or differs from the new one, or whose stored length differs, it returns -EINVAL (after the error cleanup) if the new length is below vb->planes[plane].min_length; otherwise, if the plane had a mem_priv it sets reacquired (calling buf_cleanup and clearing vb->copied_timestamp only if reacquired was not already true) and releases it with put_userptr, clears that plane's mem_priv, bytesused, length, m.userptr and data_offset, and acquires new memory with get_userptr, storing its mem_priv or returning PTR_ERR after the error cleanup. Planes unchanged by the comparison are skipped. It then copies bytesused, length, m.userptr and data_offset from the new planes into every vb->planes[plane]; if reacquired it calls buf_init and, on error, goes to the error cleanup without calling buf_cleanup; then it calls buf_prepare and, on error, calls buf_cleanup and goes to the error cleanup. It returns 0 on success. The error cleanup calls put_userptr on every plane with a non-NULL mem_priv and clears each plane's mem_priv, m.userptr and length (bytesused and data_offset are left as they then are). Returned errors: the fill_vb2_buffer error, -EINVAL, PTR_ERR from get_userptr, the buf_init error or the buf_prepare error.
note: Reviewer round 15 is right: reacquired is initialised true when plane 0 has no mem_priv, so buf_init can run (dump lines 4755-4761) without buf_cleanup or the copied_timestamp reset; old prose said buf_init ran only after a reacquire with cleanup. Also old prose said the failure path 'leaves bytesused and data_offset at whatever values they had': for a plane that reached the release step they were already zeroed (4724, 4727). buf_init failure path does not call buf_cleanup (4762-4765). name: __vb2_wait_for_done_vb
prose: Precondition: q is a valid vb2_queue; the caller holds the driver lock (q->lock or the lock managed by the wait_prepare/wait_finish ops) as for the other vb2 entry points; nonblocking tells whether the call may sleep. Postcondition: no buffer is removed from q->done_list. It loops, and in each pass tests in this order: it returns -EBUSY if q->waiting_in_dqbuf is set; -EINVAL if q->streaming is clear; -EIO if q->error is set; -EPIPE if q->last_buffer_dequeued is set; leaves the loop and returns 0 if q->done_list is non-empty; returns -EAGAIN if nonblocking is set (and the list is empty). Otherwise it sets q->waiting_in_dqbuf = 1, releases the driver lock (wait_prepare, or mutex_unlock(q->lock) if there is no wait_prepare and q->lock is set), sleeps with wait_event_interruptible until done_list is non-empty, streaming stops or q->error is set, takes the lock again (wait_finish, or mutex_lock(q->lock)), resets q->waiting_in_dqbuf to 0 and, if the sleep returned a non-zero value (interrupted), returns that value, otherwise repeats the tests. So a 0 return means that in the last pass waiting_in_dqbuf was clear, the queue was streaming without error and without last_buffer_dequeued, and done_list was non-empty. The driver lock is held on return (it is released only for the sleep and reacquired before any return).
note: Reviewer round 15 ('returns 0 with waiting_in_dqbuf set when done_list non-empty; -EBUSY only if done_list empty') is wrong: videobuf2-core.c:4817-4820 (dump) tests waiting_in_dqbuf first, before the done_list test, in every pass. Rounds 1-2 asked for -EINVAL, -EIO, -EAGAIN and -EPIPE: all present in the old prose and kept. Real source line 1982 of the file.
